title: The inhabited-universe situation
statement: The corpus situates the Elohim-civilization hypothesis within science's own possibility-space: as a concrete instance of directed panspermia in the Crick-Orgel sense — life on Earth deliberately sown by an advanced civilization — against the background of the plurality-of-worlds tradition from Greek atomism through the Sagan-Shklovskii survey to the exoplanet era, which is what makes the agent side of the hypothesis non-extraordinary as a category; the situation claim is taxonomic, not evidential — the sciences named supply a slot, not a verdict, and none of their practitioners are enlisted.

includes: The taxonomic identification: the hypothesis (woh-claim-0001) is a directed-panspermia instance — the corpus names the scientific category it falls under, at the category's own grade

The plurality background registered at documentary strength: the tradition's continuity from atomism through Arrhenius's panspermia and the mid-century SETI surveys (the Sagan-Shklovskii book that fed Sendy's program among them) to exoplanet statistics

The division of labor with woh-claim-0065: that record supplies mechanism-availability (life can be engineered), this one agent-category availability (seeding civilizations are a scientific category, not a contradiction); both yield coherence, neither yields confirmation
The honesty clause: Crick and Orgel proposed directed panspermia tentatively and without the framework's specifics, and Crick's own later assessment of its speculative standing is registered in full
excludes: The situation as evidence: occupying a slot in science's possibility-space confirms nothing, and no probability argument (Drake-style or otherwise) is run for the hypothesis
Enlistment of astrobiology, SETI, or any named scientist for the framework
The mechanism side, which is woh-claim-0065's territory
Origin-of-life adjudication; the corpus does not argue that terrestrial abiogenesis failed, only that the canon asserts design

source_references.locator: The 1973 Icarus paper proposing deliberate seeding by an advanced civilization — the category the corpus's hypothesis instantiates
Arrhenius's 1908 panspermia proposal as the tradition's earlier scientific articulation, which Crick-Orgel's directed variant presupposes
Crick's fuller statement and his own assessment of the hypothesis's speculative standing, carried as the deflationary control

alternatives.statement: A category is cheap shelter: directed panspermia is itself marginal and unfalsifiable by its proposers' admission, so situating the hypothesis within it borrows respectability from a slot science keeps only as a curiosity.
The plurality tradition makes visitors conceivable everywhere and evidence of them nowhere; a background that permits everything selects nothing, including the framework.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0001 is revised or retired.
Public prose runs a probability argument or treats the taxonomic slot as evidential support, both of which this record excludes.
The scientific standing of directed panspermia materially changes in either direction.
